title: Data types and strings
general:
Read the task: it says what to do, what the result must be and where to look. Under the task there is a Help tab: the first item is the Lesson, then steps with examples. The way to solve the task is not written in the help; you find it yourself.
Type your code in the field. Grey lines with a lock cannot be changed. Press Run: the result appears in the console. You can try as many times as you like, it does not count as an attempt. When the result is what the task asks for, press Check: the program says correct or incorrect and shows what you got. It never shows the right answer.
If the field already contains a line, first press Run and look at what it prints, then change it.

help.h: Lesson: data types and strings (Al Sweigart's book, chapter 1)
help.t:
**Data type** is the kind of a value. Whole numbers: `-2`, `30`. Numbers with a dot: `3.14`, `42.0`. Strings: text in quotes, for example `'Hello'`; the quote at the start and at the end is the same. An empty string is two quotes in a row: `''`. If you forget the closing quote, Python writes SyntaxError.
The same sign works differently depending on the values. A plus between two strings **joins** them: `'Alice' + 'Bob'` gives AliceBob; a space is not added by itself. A star between a string and a whole number **repeats** the string: `'Alice' * 5` gives AliceAliceAliceAliceAlice.
Python does not understand other combinations and writes TypeError: a string plus a number (`'Alice' + 42`), a string times a string, a string times a number with a dot. This is not a breakage, it is a message that the sign does not fit these values.
How to study: first read the lesson, then repeat the examples by hand (it is remembered better), then fix the ready code, and finally write your own.

In the examples you see program code. Lines with an arrow → are what the program prints to the console; you do not type them. Everything after the sign `#` is a comment: a note for people. Python skips it and you do not type it. Lines with a lock 🔒 are the ready part. Every task has such a part: it is shown in grey next to the field and cannot be changed. It prints the result to the console like in a real program. How it works will be explained in a separate lesson. Every example works on its own: you can run it from scratch.

In the task you write only the expression itself. Here an expression is texts with signs between them, for example `'a' + 'b'`. Around the expression there are two ready lines: `print(` above and `)` below. Together with the expression they show the result in the console. Press Run: the result appears in the console. Press Check when the solution is ready.
help.code:
| print(            # ready part: opens the output
'a' + 'b'   # the expression: two texts
| )                # ready part: closes the output
→ ab

help.t: Text is written in quotes: single 'like this' or double "like this". The quote at the start and at the end must be the same. Quotes are needed only in the code: they tell Python that this is text. There will be no quotes in the console. Any sign inside quotes is just part of the text, like a letter: `'@'`, `'*'`, `'-'`, `'.'`.
help.code:
| print(            # ready part: opens the output
'Hello'   # text in quotes
| )                # ready part: closes the output
→ Hello

help.h: 3. A space and an empty text
help.t: A space inside quotes is also part of the text. It counts as an ordinary sign. An empty text is two quotes in a row with nothing between them: `''`.
help.code:
| print(            # ready part: opens the output
'Good morning'   # text with a space between the words
| )                # ready part: closes the output
→ Good morning

help.t: The sign `+` joins two texts into one. A space is not added by itself: if it is needed, it is written as a separate text `' '`.
help.code:
| print(            # ready part: the first output
'Home' + 'work'   # joined two texts without a space
| )                # ready part: end of the first output
| print(            # ready part: the second output
'Home' + ' ' + 'work'   # joined three texts: word, space, word
| )                # ready part: end of the second output
→ Homework
→ Home work

help.h: 5. The star sign with a text and a number
help.t: The sign `*` repeats a text as many times as the number says. The number must be whole and is written without quotes.
help.code:
| print(            # ready part: opens the output
'Yes' * 3   # the text 'Yes' repeated 3 times
| )                # ready part: closes the output
| print(            # ready part: the second output
'+' * 4   # a plus in quotes is an ordinary sign: it was repeated 4 times
| )                # ready part: end of the second output
→ YesYesYes
→ ++++

help.t: Python does `*` first, then `+`. Parentheses change the order: what is in parentheses is done first.
help.code:
| print(            # ready part: opens the output
'Yes' * 2 + '!'   # first 'Yes' * 2 = 'YesYes', then + '!'
| )                # ready part: closes the output
→ YesYes!

help.t:
Python says `TypeError` when a sign does not fit these data types. This is not a breakage, it is a message. Causes: multiplying text by text, multiplying text by a number with a dot, adding text and a number.
• Wrong: `'Yes' * 'Yes'` (text times text).
• Right: `'Yes' * 2` (text times a whole number).
What to check: what is on the left and on the right of the sign, whether it is text or a number, whether there are extra quotes around a number. The last line of the message says exactly what is wrong. The line above shows the place in the program where it happened.
help.code:
| print(            # ready part: opens the output
'Yes' * 'Yes'   # error: text cannot be multiplied by text
| )                # ready part: closes the output
→ Traceback (most recent call last):
→   File "solution.py", line 2, in <module>
→     'Yes' * 'Yes'
→ TypeError: can't multiply sequence by non-int of type 'str'

questions.text:
What to do: type `'Alice' + 'Bob'` in the field and press Run. This is an example from the lesson (type the quotes too).
Expected result: the console shows `AliceBob`.
Where to look: Help, "Lesson".

What to do: type `'Alice' * 5` in the field and press Run. This is an example from the lesson (type the quotes too).
Expected result: the console shows `AliceAliceAliceAliceAlice`.
Where to look: Help, "Lesson".

What to do: print one text made of three parts: `anna`, `@` and `mail.com`.
Expected result: the console shows `anna@mail.com`, without spaces.
Where to look: Help, "Lesson", steps 2 and 4.
questions.about: Practice: working with text in quotes.

Expected result: the console shows `Anna Smith`.
Where to look: Help, "Lesson", steps 3 and 4.
